rule: pen visibly closes into one or more full loops on the strip (a repeated double hump, like a cursive w)
pen visibly closes into a chain of small loops (a repeated wave, like cursive mmmm/nnnn)
a closed loop (P-shaped) with a stem below it -- the loop closure is the feature a reader catches first
a simple open curve (C-shaped), no closure, no tail reaching below the line
a small open comma-shaped hook, tail curls but the stroke neither closes into a loop nor drops below the line
a thin open S-curve stroke, no full loop closure, no clear descender below the line
an open hook (7-shaped) whose stroke drops clearly below the line
a J/3-shaped open hook whose stroke drops clearly below the line
a tall stroke combining a hook top with a long descender/tail below the line
